#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
# dx run-gate — run one heavy command under host-wide admission
#
# A project gate, a test suite or a build is the work that takes a shared
# machine down when several sessions start one at the same moment.
# This is the sanctioned way to run one: it takes a `heavy` lease so at most a
# host-appropriate number run at once, waits with a heartbeat that says who is
# ahead and for how long, runs the command at reduced scheduling priority under
# the session's process token, streams its output to a session-owned log, and
# records the result.
#
# It never discards a completed result. A gate that ran is evidence about the
# tree it ran on, whether it passed or failed, and the receipt is what stops
# the next phase paying for the same answer.
set -euo pipefail

source "${DEX_DIR:-$HOME/work/dex}/lib/common.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage: dx run-gate [options] [--] <command> [args...]

Run one heavy command — a project gate, a test suite, a build — under
host-wide admission, at reduced priority, owned by this session. A dev server
is not a gate: start it directly; it is session-owned without a lease.

At most DEX_MAX_ACTIVE_HEAVY heavy commands run at once across every Dex
session on this host. The default is derived from the host: one per four
cores and per eight gigabytes, whichever is fewer, at least one. While the
pool is full this waits and prints how many owners are ahead and how long the
oldest has been running; waiting never fails the command.

Output streams to a log under this session's temp root and is replayed when
the command finishes, so a long gate can be started from one tool call and
polled from the next. The process dies with the session.

Options:
  --name <name>       Receipt name for this gate (default: derived from the
                      command). One receipt per name per session.
  --timeout <secs>    Stop the command after this many seconds; 0 means no
                      deadline (default: DEX_GATE_TIMEOUT, or 0)
  -h, --help          Show this help

Exit status is the command's own, or:
  2   bad arguments, or an unsafe capacity pool
  70  Dex could not prepare the gate (log, lease, or receipt)
USAGE
}

GATE_NAME=""
GATE_TIMEOUT="${DEX_GATE_TIMEOUT:-0}"
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    --name)
      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { dx_error "--name needs a value"; exit 2; }

input.content:
# csv-rfc4180

A CSV parser and serializer for Node.js, with no dependencies. It follows RFC 4180 and also accepts LF and CR line endings. It can parse a whole string or input that arrives in chunks.

```js
const { parse, createParser, stringify, CsvError } = require('csv-rfc4180');

parse('name,age\r\nAda,36\r\n');
// [['name', 'age'], ['Ada', '36']]

parse('name,age\nAda,36\n', { header: true });
// [{ name: 'Ada', age: '36' }]

stringify([['a,b', 'say "hi"'], ['']]);
// '"a,b","say ""hi"""\r\n""\r\n'
```

Run the tests with `npm test`.

## `parse(text, options)`

Returns an array of records. Each record is an array of strings, or an object when `header` is `true`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delimiter` | `','` | One UTF-16 code unit, other than `"`, CR or LF. |
| `header` | `false` | The first record names the columns and later records become objects. |
| `skipEmptyLines` | `false` | Drop lines with no characters at all. Without it, each such line is the record `['']`. |

- Records end at CRLF, LF or CR. A single line break at the end of the input does not start another record.
- A leading byte order mark is dropped. Columns in error positions are counted from after it.
- Fields are never trimmed. A `"` only starts a quoted field when it is the field's first character.
- In header mode, duplicate column names and records with the wrong number of fields are errors. Records are plain objects. A column named `__proto__` becomes an ordinary own key. Integer-like column names come first in `Object.keys` order, as with any JavaScript object.

Bad arguments throw `TypeError`. Malformed input throws `CsvError`, whose `line` and `column` (1-based, in UTF-16 code units) point to:

| Error | Position |
| --- | --- |
| Quoted field never closed | its opening `"` |
| Anything other than a delimiter or line break after a closing `"` | that character |
| Duplicate header name | the start of the second occurrence |
| Wrong field count in header mode | column 1 of the line where the record starts |

If the input has several errors, you get the first one met reading left to right. A duplicate header name is detected when that header field ends. A field count is checked when the record ends.

## `createParser(options)`

A streaming parser. It takes the same options as `parse`.

```js
const parser = createParser({ header: true });
parser.write('id,na');     // []
parser.write('me\n1,x\n'); // [{ id: '1', name: 'x' }]
parser.end();              // []
```

`write(chunk)` returns the records whose ending line break is in that chunk. `end()` returns whatever is left. After `end()`, or once either method has thrown, both methods throw. However the input is split, the records and errors are the same as `parse` gives for the whole input. Each code unit is read once, and the parser keeps only the record it is currently reading.

## `stringify(rows, options)`

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delimiter` | `','` | Same rules as for `parse`. |
| `eol` | `'\r\n'` | `'\r\n'` or `'\n'`. Every record ends with it, including the last one. |
| `header` | none | An array of column names. It is written first, and object records are written in its order. A key the object does not own is written as an empty field. |

Strings are written as they are. Numbers and booleans go through `String()`. `null` and `undefined` become empty fields. Any other value throws `TypeError`.

A field is quoted when it contains the delimiter, `"`, CR or LF, or when it starts or ends with a space. A record whose only field is empty is written as `""`, so `skipEmptyLines` cannot drop it. When `header` is set but `rows` is empty, only the header line is written.

`parse(stringify(rows, opts), opts)` returns `rows` for any rows that are non-empty arrays of strings. To make that hold, one rule goes beyond the list above: if the output would start with U+FEFF, the first field is quoted, because otherwise `parse` would drop it as a byte order mark.

content.text:
I've built the CSV parser and serializer, and all 119 tests pass, including one full run through the Dex gate (`full-gate`, 12s).

**Files**
- `src/csv.js`: exports `parse`, `createParser`, `stringify` and `CsvError`. `parse` runs the streaming parser over the whole string, so the two can't give different results.
- `package.json`: `npm test` runs `node --test test/*.test.js`. No dependencies.
- `test/`: one file each for `parse`, `createParser`, `stringify` and round trips, plus a check that `require('csv-rfc4180')` loads `src/csv.js`.
- `README.md`: usage and the error positions. I ran its examples to confirm the outputs it shows.

**Verification**
- **Chunk splitting:** for 18 awkward inputs under 5 option sets, the streaming parser matches `parse` at every 2-chunk and 3-chunk split point, one character at a time, and on 3,000 random inputs. That covers records, errors, positions and messages.
- **Round trip:** `parse(stringify(rows, opts), opts)` returns the same rows for 4,000 random tables under 8 option sets, and for 1,000 more fed to the streaming parser in chunks.
- **Speed:** one test does 300,000 one-character writes and would time out if earlier input were re-read. On 12.7 MB, parse and stream each took about 100 ms.
- **Tests can fail:** I broke the code five ways on purpose, and each break made between 1 and 20 tests fail. The tests also caught a real bug: an empty last header field (input `,`) was reported at column 1 instead of column 2. That is fixed.

**Where I had to choose** (also in the README)
- **Duplicate headers:** a duplicate name is reported as soon as its field ends. So `a,a,"b` reports the duplicate, not the unclosed quote.
- **Wrong field count:** the error gives the line where the record starts, for records that span several lines.
- **BOM:** columns are counted from after a leading BOM.
- **Extra stringify rule:** if the output would start with a BOM character (U+FEFF), the first field is quoted. Without this the round trip breaks, because `parse` would drop it. The spec's quoting list doesn't mention it.
- **Header with no rows:** `stringify([], { header })` writes the header line rather than `''`.
- **`[null]`:** it is written as `""`, the same as `['']`.
- **Missing keys:** only keys the object owns are read, so with a header of `['toString']` an empty object writes an empty field instead of throwing.
- **Delimiter:** it must be a single UTF-16 code unit, so an emoji throws `TypeError`.
- **Option types:** `parse` throws `TypeError` if `header` or `skipEmptyLines` isn't a boolean. It ignores options it doesn't use, such as `eol`, so one options object can go to both functions.

**Guidelines I didn't follow as written**
- **Linting:** there's no linter, since adding one would bring in dependencies. I ran `node --check` on every file instead.
- **Humanizer:** that skill isn't available in this session, so I wrote the README without it.
- **Node versions:** `engines` says Node 18 or later, but I only tested on Node 24.
- **Git:** the work is committed on branch `feat/csv-parser`. There's no remote, so nothing was pushed. A hook asked for conventional commit messages and a Dex co-author line, so the commits use those. `CLAUDE.md` is still untracked.

**Possible follow-ups (not built)**
- `stringify` could reject duplicate header names, since `parse` rejects them.
- Records keyed by a `Map`, so column names like `1` keep their header order.
- A Node stream `Transform` wrapper around `createParser`.
